summary: Reads Word .docx documents and turns the paragraphs and tables into one searchable text record.
purpose: Makes the text of a Word document searchable as one unit.
why: Likely reason: treating the whole document as one record is the simplest way to search it. Reason not stated.
how: The document is opened and each paragraph with text is collected. Each table is turned into lines with separators and added as a numbered block. Everything is joined into one text block and stored as one record with paragraph and table counts. The result is logged and returned. Errors are logged and passed back.
inputs: A path to a .docx or .doc file.
outputs: A list with one parsed record. Its file type is word, and its metadata holds the paragraph and table counts.
risks: The .doc ending is listed, but this library reads only .docx, so old files will probably fail. All paragraphs come before all tables, so the original reading order is lost. A long document becomes one large record with no page numbers. An empty document still produces a record with empty text.
debug: If a .doc file fails, save it as .docx and try again. If table content appears far from where it belongs, that is the ordering issue. If an empty record shows up, check the source file.
